translation.title: Minoxidil 3% Gel
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used to treat male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) and female-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).
translation.usage: Men: after drying the hair and scalp completely, apply 0.5 to 1 g to the affected scalp area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months; do not exceed a total of 2 g per day. Women: after drying the hair and scalp completely, apply 0.5 g to the affected scalp area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months; do not exceed a total of 1.3 g per day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you are pregnant, possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, if you are under 18 years old, if you have cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, heart valve disease, or treated or untreated high or low blood pressure), if your hair loss has no hereditary (genetic) factor, if you have sudden patchy hair loss or hair loss of unknown cause, if your scalp is abnormal (redness, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain, psoriasis, sunburn), if you have shaved your scalp, or if your hair loss is related to childbirth. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are elderly. If you forget an application, do not make up the missed dose; simply apply the next dose as scheduled. This medicine is for external use only - do not apply it to any area other than the scalp. Do not use an occlusive (sealed) dressing over it. It can cause burning and irritation of the eyes, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it touches the eyes, broken skin or mucous membranes, rinse immediately with plenty of clean water. Wash your hands thoroughly after each use. Use hair styling products only after this medicine has dried; when applying in the evening, apply it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so it can dry. Do not use a hair dryer to speed up drying. Do not use it together with other scalp medicines, topical corticosteroids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol, or medicines known to enhance absorption through the skin; consult a doctor or pharmacist before using it with vasodilators such as guanethidine. Stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if you notice itching, scaling, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, unwanted hair growth outside the application area (including facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including burning and rash, peeling, hair loss, acne, nail disorders, seborrhea or eczema, or - occasionally - diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, changes in blood pressure or pulse, palpitations, a faster heartbeat, dizziness, headache, light-headedness, fainting, swelling (edema), or sudden unexplained weight gain. Hair loss may recur after you stop using this medicine. Store at room temperature away from moisture and light, keep out of reach of children, and keep away from open flames.
